// diagnostic

E0175

`#State` markers on `{type}` are retired

What

`#State` markers on `{type}` are retired

Why

State types carry these facts: a parameter typed `{type}.A` requires `A`, a result typed `{type}.B` moves the value to `B`, and the state list names each move as `A -> B`

Fix

Run `jet fix` to write each marker's states into its signature and its moves into the state list of `{type}`

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0175: tests/ui/typestate/qualified_state_markers_seed_leaf_states.stderr.

Error [jet.TypestateMarkerRetired]: `#State` markers on `Door` are retired
  --> tests/ui/typestate/qualified_state_markers_seed_leaf_states.jet:5:5
    |
  5 |     #State(_ -> Door.State.Closed) new: fn() -[]> Door { return Door{} }
    |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: State types carry these facts: a parameter typed `Owner.A` requires `A`, a result typed `Owner.B` moves the value to `B`, and the owner's state list names each move as `A -> B`
 Fix: Run `jet fix` to write each marker's states into its signature and its moves into the state list of `Door`
